narrative.overview:
Poster is a desk where one person prepares a batch of posts, checks every one, and sends the set off. The design is calm, precise and trustworthy: these posts go out under the owner's name, so nothing on screen may surprise them or overstate itself. Sheet-white cards sit on a pale Desk Grey background, one card per station on the desk: adding images, the gallery, AI content and scheduling, scheduled posts, and the activity log. A single line above the cards reads like a dispatch slip: how many images, how many have captions, how many still need a publish time, how many are ready, and what Buffer holds. Hairlines separate everything, and colour is held back for two jobs. Dispatch Indigo marks the next action, the current selection and focus. Four status colours report what has happened.

The density is that of a working tool, not a landing page. Text is 12–15px, controls are 26–38px tall, and status is visible at all times: the mode badge and service labels in the header, the batch line, counts on every action button, progress on every run. The work runs top to bottom in the order it happens: generate captions, plan the times, schedule. Numbers are exact and use tabular figures. Light and dark themes are both first-class. Every colour is a CSS custom property, redefined for dark under `[data-theme="dark"]` in `static/css/poster.css`.

Poster rejects three looks: growth-hacker SaaS (gradients, glows, purple-to-pink washes, sparkle decoration), copies of the social networks it posts to (Instagram, X, Buffer's own UI), and analytics dashboards (charts, trend arrows, hero metrics that suggest measured performance).
keyCharacteristics: One flat accent, Dispatch Indigo, used only for the next action, selection and focus.
Four status colours (green, amber, red, blue), each paired with a label or icon.
Flat cards with 1px hairlines. Real shadows appear only on layers that float.
The operating system's UI font, small and dense, with tabular numbers everywhere.
Rounded rectangles that grow with size (6 → 16px), and pills for status.
No gradients and no coloured glow anywhere.
Light and dark themes built from the same tokens.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Dispatch Indigo means "act here" or "this is selected". There is one next action per stage, and only it is filled indigo. In the AI panel that is **All images** while posts lack captions, **Apply to all** while posts need a time, and **All ready** while posts are ready; when the batch is done, nothing in the panel is indigo. Once every image has a caption, **All images** can only replace them, so it becomes a ghost **Regenerate all**. The editor's **Schedule post** is never indigo. The indigo button is also the one Ctrl+Shift+Enter (⌘ on a Mac) presses: it carries `aria-keyshortcuts` and a "Next step" tooltip, and a folded planner opens rather than applying. Dialogs and the Settings drawer each have their own single primary (**Save settings**). Never use indigo as decoration or as a background for a whole region.

rules.name: The Status Speaks Twice Rule
rules.body: A status colour never stands alone. Chips carry a dot and text, service labels carry a dot and a name, log lines carry a category tag tinted by level (errors also use red text), banners carry an icon and a title, and the batch line's "need a publish time" is words as well as amber. List items never get a coloured side stripe.

rules.name: The Flat Colour Rule
rules.body: Every fill is one flat colour. No gradients, including on the brand mark and progress bars, and no coloured glow.

rules.name: The Estimate Is Not a Metric Rule
rules.body: The engagement score is the model's guess. It is shown as plain "89 / 100" text with the words "estimate" and "not a measurement", never with a slider, a colour scale or success-green.

rules.name: The System Voice Rule
rules.body: Poster ships no web fonts. Its Content Security Policy only allows files from its own server, so a new face would have to be self-hosted and justified. Use `var(--font)` and `var(--mono)`.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: Every count, counter, score, position, time and duration uses `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`. This covers the batch line, count badges, button counts, character counters, the estimate, "3 of 12", the gallery card's time line and op stats.

rules.name: The In-Between Weights Note
rules.body: Weights 550, 650 and 750 render exactly only with variable system fonts (Segoe UI Variable, SF Pro). Elsewhere they round to the nearest available weight. That's acceptable, but never rely on 650 versus 700 to carry meaning.

rules.name: The South Asian Script Rule
rules.body: Captions and hashtags in Bengali, Hindi, Tamil and other South Asian scripts are normal content. Text that shows a post's words is 13px or larger with a line-height of at least 1.5, and never clips vertically. Poster sets `lang` from the script of the text (bn, hi, ta and others), so screen readers use the right voice and the browser picks the right font. The system stack falls back to Nirmala UI on Windows and the Sangam or Kohinoor faces on Apple. Don't set a font stack that blocks those fallbacks. Text is shortened only between whole graphemes, and hashtags keep the zero-width joiner and non-joiner.

rules.name: The Hairline First Rule
rules.body: Separate things with a 1px Hairline or a tonal step before reaching for a shadow. A shadow at rest never exceeds Whisper, and no shadow is ever coloured. Fields are the exception to the hairline: their edge is Field Edge, because it has to be seen.

dos: **Do** take every colour from the CSS custom properties, and define any new colour in both the light (`:root, [data-theme="light"]`) and dark (`[data-theme="dark"]`) blocks.
**Do** give each action group exactly one primary (Dispatch Indigo) button. Everything else is default, ghost or danger.
**Do** pair every status colour with a label, dot or icon (The Status Speaks Twice Rule).
**Do** use tabular numbers for every count, counter, score and time.
**Do** offer the caption language as an instruction to the model, never as a promise: Poster does not claim a draft is in the language asked for.
**Do** build new panels as a card with a header row, a hairline and a 20px body, on 14px corners with the Whisper shadow.
**Do** show a post's own words at 13px or larger with a line-height of at least 1.5, and set `lang` from its script.
**Do** keep the 2px focus outline (or the 3px field ring) on everything interactive, and keep reduced-motion support.
**Do** keep Muted Slate for any secondary text that has to be read; it passes 4.5:1 everywhere.
**Do** say "Demo mode (not in Buffer)" wherever Demo results are reported, and nowhere else more than once: in Demo the service labels are hidden and the AI panel says "(simulated)".
**Do** count posts the way the owner does, one per image, and give Buffer's per-channel count in brackets.

**Do** give each post one editor: a post from the open gallery is edited in the post editor (Edit in Buffer, also from its row in Scheduled posts); only a post from elsewhere uses the Scheduled-post dialog. Write every Buffer edit back into the draft, so the batch and Buffer never disagree.
**Do** show time zones under their current IANA names (Asia/Kolkata, not Asia/Calcutta).
donts: **Don't** drift into growth-hacker SaaS: no gradients, glows, purple-to-pink washes or decorative sparkles. The sparkles icon labels AI generation actions and is never used as ornament.
**Don't** imitate Instagram, X or Buffer's interface. The post preview shows the text plainly, not as a fake network card.

**Don't** turn Poster into an analytics dashboard: no charts, trend arrows, hero numbers or KPI tiles. The batch line counts the work, and the engagement score is always presented as the model's estimate.
**Don't** fill a button red. Destructive actions are outlined red, confirmed in a dialog, and the dialog opens with Cancel focused.
**Don't** use Faint Slate for text. It's for icons, grips and dots.
**Don't** call a post "Ready" unless it has a caption and a publish time ahead.
**Don't** load fonts, icons or styles from another origin. The Content Security Policy forbids it, and the icon sprite lives in `templates/index.html`.
**Don't** raise resting shadows above Whisper, or colour a shadow.
**Don't** give list items or alerts a coloured side stripe.
**Don't** disable a post that is in Buffer to lock it: make its fields read-only, so its words stay readable and in the Tab order.
**Don't** show a toast while a modal is open, or pair a toast with opening one: it sits under the backdrop. Say it in the drawer or dialog.
